issues.description: TurnDetectionMode and EndOfUtteranceMode are two parallel enums complecting the same concept
issues.detail: The code now branches on both TurnDetectionMode and EndOfUtteranceMode (with matching FIXED/EXTERNAL members) to derive _enable_vad. These are two names for one underlying concern: who finalizes the turn. The mapping between them is implicit and place-oriented (a boolean cached at init time), rather than a single value describing the turn-control regime. Decompose into one explicit enum of turn-control values, or derive _enable_vad lazily from a single source of truth.

issues.description: Default mode change is a silent behavior swap for existing callers
issues.detail: Flipping the default from EXTERNAL to FIXED changes time semantics for every existing caller that didn't pass turn_detection_mode explicitly. The value of 'what finalizes a turn' has changed without the caller's input changing. This is exactly the kind of identity/time confusion that bites later: same construction expression, different behavior across versions. At minimum the changelog 'fixed' entry should be 'changed' (breaking default), and ideally the default should be None with explicit resolution logged.

issues.description: split_sentences is complected: param-level bool, config-level emit_sentences, plus an always-on SpeechSegmentConfig assignment
issues.detail: The new parameter is named split_sentences in InputParams, translated to emit_sentences on SpeechSegmentConfig, and the SpeechSegmentConfig is unconditionally constructed even when the user passed nothing (params.split_sentences or False). Three names for one fact, and a forced default that overwrites whatever the SDK's own default would have been. Either pass the value through with one name, or only set speech_segment_config when the user actually specified it. The 'or False' coerces None to a meaningful False, which is a value/identity confusion.

issues.description: Frame-type branching now warns on a frame the service explicitly subscribed to
issues.detail: process_frame logs a warning when VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame arrives and _enable_vad is True. If internal VAD is being used, the upstream pipeline arguably shouldn't be sending this frame at all; if it does, a warning per frame is noisy and not actionable. This is essential vs. incidental: the essential question is 'who owns endpointing for this turn', and the answer should be decided at one place, not re-litigated on every frame with a log line.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics line moved but not deleted
issues.detail: The `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` line was relocated from after the broadcast/interruption calls to before them, still commented out. Dead code carrying an implicit ordering claim is exactly the kind of incidental noise that accumulates. Either the metric belongs at one specific point and should be uncommented, or it should be removed.

issues.description: _prepare_config uses a string list + getattr/setattr/hasattr loop
issues.detail: The list of attribute names with hasattr/setattr is an 'easy' pattern (familiar) that is not simple: it loses static checkability, hides which fields are actually supported by the SDK version, and the new 'split_sentences' entry both flows through this loop and is set explicitly via SpeechSegmentConfig a few lines later. Pick one mechanism. A plain dataclass or explicit assignments would make the value flow obvious and version drift easier to spot.

review.summary: The change is small but it deepens an existing complecting in the service: two parallel mode enums (TurnDetectionMode, EndOfUtteranceMode) both encode 'who finalizes a turn', and the new FIXED member is added to both without unifying them. The default flip from EXTERNAL to FIXED silently changes the time semantics of every existing caller; that is a values-and-time issue dressed as a fix. The new split_sentences parameter is reasonable but is renamed mid-flight (split_sentences -> emit_sentences) and the SpeechSegmentConfig is constructed unconditionally with an 'or False' coercion, which conflates 'not specified' with 'explicitly false'. The right hammock-time question is: what is the single value that describes turn control here, and where does it live? Decompose that first, then the frame routing and the warning become obvious data, not branching code.
